title: Biome Health Project Maasai Mara 2018
description: Field survey imagery collected by the Biome Health Project in the Maasai Mara ecosystem during 2018. # Biome Health Project Maasai Mara 2018

### Biome Health Project Maasai Mara 2018

#### S3 base

`s3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/agentmorris/lila-wildlife/biome-health-project-maasai-mara-2018`

#### Overview

This dataset contains 37,075 images from the [WWF-UK/UCL Biome Health Project](https://www.biomehealthproject.com/) site in the Maasai Mara, Kenya. These images form the training, test, and validation sets for the [Maasai Mara Classifier model](https://github.com/omipan/camera_traps_classifier). This dataset was created by labeling one image per five-minute period across 176 camera sites.

Labels are provided for 100 categories, most of which are species, but some of which are species groups (for example, the 'shoat' category is sheep and goats combined). Labels include wild mammals, wild birds, and domestic mammals. Blank images and images containing humans have been removed.

#### Data format

Annotations (including species tags and unique location identifiers) are provided in [COCO Camera Traps](https://lila.science/coco-camera-traps) format.

For information about mapping this dataset's categories to a common taxonomy, see [this page](https://lila.science/taxonomy-mapping-for-camera-trap-data-sets/).

#### Downloading the data

Metadata is available [here](https://lilawildlife.blob.core.windows.net/lila-wildlife/biome-health-project-maasai-mara-2018/biome-health-project-maasai-mara-2018.json).

Images are available in the following cloud storage folders:

* gs://public-datasets-lila/biome-health-project-maasai-mara-2018 (GCP)
* s3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/agentmorris/lila-wildlife/biome-health-project-maasai-mara-2018 (AWS)
* https://lilawildlife.blob.core.windows.net/lila-wildlife/biome-health-project-maasai-mara-2018 (Azure)

We recommend downloading images (the whole folder, or a subset of the folder) using [gsutil](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/gsutil) (for GCP), [aws s3](https://awscli.amazonaws.com/v2/documentation/api/latest/reference/s3/index.html) (for AWS), or [AzCopy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-use-azcopy-v10) (for Azure). For more information about using gsutil, aws s3, or AzCopy, check out our [guidelines for accessing images without using giant zipfiles](http://lila.science/image-access).
